answer: Weight each identity by the maximum flow of staked trust reaching it from honest anchors, not by raw headcount. Think of trust as a prism splitting one beam: a sybil fleet hiding behind a single bribed gateway must divide that gateway's fixed staked capacity among all its clones, so a rising tide of fakes only dilutes each one toward zero weight. The fable that more identities means more power dies here. To give N fakes full standing, an attacker must buy N independent bonded trust edges from distinct honest anchors, paying N times real collateral.
